historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (47.6%) diverges from EPS CAGR (92.9%) by 45.3pp and FCF CAGR (82.2%) by 34.6pp — all metrics reflect the AI-boom inflection and are unsustainable as terminal rates. base.description: Secular AI growth continues but decelerates sharply after FY2026 ramp. NVIDIA maintains 75-80% GPU market share. Hyperscalers sustain CapEx builds but growth normalizes from current levels. FCF margin ~47% sustained.
base.wacc_rationale: 11% reflects large-cap tech beta ~1.5-1.7, risk-free rate ~4.3%, ERP ~5.5%, modest concentration/geopolitical premium

bull.description: Blackwell + Rubin architecture dominance extends. Enterprise AI adoption accelerates. CUDA moat widens further. Hyperscaler CapEx continues $200B+/yr through 2028. Networking revenue scales. WACC lower on quality premium.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10% for best-case scenario reflecting quality and secular tailwind premium

bear.description: AI capex digestion cycle. Custom silicon (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia) displaces 30-40% of NVIDIA workloads. China export controls expand, eliminating 13% of revenue. Revenue plateaus by Y3-Y4 with modest FCF decline in Y5 as pricing power erodes.
bear.wacc_rationale: 12% for elevated risk: customer concentration, custom silicon threat, regulatory headwinds, geopolitical exposure

sensitivity.notes: Rows = WACC (9% to 13%), Cols = Terminal Growth (2.0% to 4.0%). Base growth path [65%, 35%, 25%, 18%, 12%] applied uniformly. Values are intrinsic value per share.

trigger_checks.assessment: Base case IV implies P/E of 21.9x on FY26E EPS — this is BELOW the 10-year historical average of 55-65x for NVDA in growth periods and at the lower end of the full historical range (22-115x). No sanity check trigger fires. The model is conservative, not aggressive.

sanity_check.verdict: PASS — No correction applied. Base IV ($96.77) implies P/E of 21.9x on FY26E consensus EPS — well below NVDA's historical average and approaching its historical minimum. The model does not trip any high-upside warning (base case shows -51.6% downside from current price). The material gap between DCF IV ($97) and current market price ($200) is explained by: (1) Market embedding a platform-monopoly scarcity premium on CUDA ecosystem value not captured in 5-year cash flows; (2) TAM expansion to $4T+ AI infrastructure spend by 2030 lies significantly beyond the explicit 5-year window; (3) NVDA structurally commands a premium multiple reflecting 80-90% market share in mission-critical AI compute. At $200, investors are paying primarily for terminal platform value, which carries material execution and multiple-compression risk.
sanity_check.adjustment_made: None. Growth assumptions already incorporate the prompt-specified decelerating path. WACC of 11% base appropriately prices concentration, geopolitical, and execution risk. No peak-FCF mid-cycle swap applied — NVDA's growth is secular AI infrastructure driven, not cyclical-agricultural.
